title: CBEGRec: Learning Path Recommendation via Concept Bundling and Exercise Generation

problem.claim: Learning path recommendation must guide learners through structured sequences of concepts and exercises toward specific learning goals.

gap.claim: Existing methods commonly recommend isolated concepts and retrieve exercises from static banks, which may ignore concept relationships and fail to meet diverse and dynamic learner needs.

contributions.claim: CBEGRec recommends learning paths through concept bundling and exercise generation.
The Goal-oriented Concept Bundling module selects semantically coherent concept bundles using learners' current knowledge states and structural proximity to the learning goal.

The Path-aware Exercise Generation module synthesizes personalized exercises that support progressive learning and evolve with the learning path through an LLM-driven Teacher--Solver--Critic closed loop.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe CBEGRec as a novel framework for learning path recommendation via concept bundling and exercise generation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments in simulated scenarios and human evaluation validate the superiority of their method.
The authors report that code is available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Learning path recommendation guides learners through structured concept and exercise sequences toward learning goals.
Existing approaches isolate concepts and depend on finite static exercise banks, limiting attention to concept relationships and dynamic learner needs.
CBEGRec addresses these limitations with goal-oriented concept bundling based on learner knowledge and goal proximity.
Path-aware exercise generation creates personalized exercises that evolve with the learning path through a Teacher--Solver--Critic loop.
The authors report validation through simulated experiments and human evaluation, with code availability.

source_observation.claim: The abstract combines concept bundling based on learner state and goal structure with exercise generation that adapts as the path progresses.

interpretation.claim: Learning-path systems may benefit from coordinating content selection and content creation rather than treating them as separate retrieval steps.

application.claim: For adaptive learning applications, jointly model relationships among concepts, learner knowledge, learning goals, and evolving exercise needs.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach is preferable when generated exercises are unnecessary, costly, or subject to domain-specific quality constraints.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the implementation or evaluation details of the LLM-driven closed loop.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported superiority.
